question.text: Under the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR), the Indian tax authorities have powers which are relevant to AIF structuring. Which of the following describes GAAR's most relevant implication for AIF structures?

answer.text: GAAR allows authorities to re-characterise transactions on grounds of lack of commercial substance
GAAR prohibits the use of any offshore pooling jurisdiction for Indian AIFs
GAAR mandates that every AIF pool must be constituted only as a trust
GAAR is applicable only to listed companies and has no bearing on AIF structures

explanation.text: The Logic: Footnote 69 of Chapter 8 and Section 8.2 item 5 explain GAAR (effective 1 April 2017) lets authorities re-characterise transactions lacking commercial substance. Overly complex AIF structures risk GAAR challenge. The Trap: Option B is an over-statement; GAAR does not ban offshore pooling. Option C confuses GAAR with SEBI structural choice. Option D is false — GAAR applies to all structures. Cross-Exam Context: XVI (Taxation) covers GAAR in depth; XIX-C focuses on GAAR's fund-structuring implications, especially substance-over-form tests. Manager's Pro-Tip: When selecting a feeder jurisdiction, ensure there is demonstrable commercial substance — office, staff, board meetings abroad — to avoid GAAR re-characterisation that could collapse DTAA benefits.
